messages.subject: WLSMV multiple groups 'measurementInvariance'
parts:
Dear all,
I am doing a multiple groups analysis and I fitted the model using WLSMV and the cfa function with the group argument, but I didn't declare my variables as ordered, because not every category of every variable was used in each group, so I felt I needed to treat the variables (range 0-4) as continuous. One of the ML options didn't seem as an alternative to me, because I wanted to use missing="pairwise" and the variables are slightly skewed and kurtotic. The next step was to use the function measurementInvariance to investigate the next steps, but it seems like there will be no option to use WLSMV, just DWLS if I am correct? The same for doing it step by step and then using the anova function. Is there an option to use WLSMV?
Thank you very much in advance! Your help is very appreciated!
Theresa

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: WLSMV multiple groups 'measurementInvariance'
parts: I needed to treat the variables (range 0-4) as continuous.

This paper suggests that may be viable, since you have 5 categories:

http://psych.colorado.edu/~willcutt/pdfs/Rhemtulla_2012.pdf

The paper does not investigate missing data though, nor multigroup models or invariance.
One of the ML options didn't seem as an alternative to me, because I wanted to use missing="pairwise" and the variables are slightly skewed and kurtotic.
Using MLR corrects SEs and chi-squared for nonnormality, with near-nominal Type I error rates according to the paper above.  And using MLR allows you to set missing = "FIML"
The next step was to use the function measurementInvariance to investigate the next steps, but it seems like there will be no option to use WLSMV, just DWLS if I am correct?

WLSMV is the DWLS estimator, along with robust standard errors and a mean (M) and variance (V) adjusted chi-squared.  But if you are treating your data as continuous, you can use robust ML (MLR).
